tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 unhealthy in production — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions immediately after the v2.3.1 deploy. Observed error rate was 18% (baseline ~0.2%) with all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) on v2.3.1 and reporting unhealthy.

Remediation: rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0, the most recent release with a healthy status in production (release history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc was a staging release and also unhealthy). The first rollback attempt halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving the fleet in a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0, us-west/eu-west still on v2.3.1). A retry of the rollback to v2.3.0 completed across all regions.

Current state: all three regions on v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate 0.2%. Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is not yet identified — follow-up investigation needed before any re-deploy of v2.3.1. v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so a change-manager approval would be required for any future deploy of that version.

trace.final:
Done. Summary:

**Rollback**
- Found checkout-api on **v2.3.1** in all three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy with an 18% error rate.
- Release history showed v2.2.9 (healthy), v2.3.0 (healthy), v2.3.1 (unhealthy), and v2.3.1-rc (staging, unhealthy). The most recent release healthy in production was **v2.3.0**.
- First rollback to v2.3.0 halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a mixed state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west/eu-west still on v2.3.1). I retried and it completed across all regions.
- Verified: all regions on v2.3.0, service **healthy**, error rate back to ~0.2%.

**Incident**
- Opened **INC-0001**, SEV2, for checkout-api, paging on-call. The summary documents the failure, the rollback (including the partial-failure/retry), and the current healthy state, plus a note that v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production so any future deploy of it needs change-manager approval.
- Note: the first incident-creation call timed out; I retried with the same idempotency key, so only one incident exists.

Root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures is still unidentified — worth investigating before reattempting that version.

transcript.content: I'll start by checking the current status and release history for checkout-api.

Current state: all three regions are on v2.3.1 (unhealthy, 18% error rate). The most recent production release that was healthy is **v2.3.0** (v2.3.1-rc is a staging release, and it's unhealthy anyway). Rolling back to v2.3.0:
transcript.reasoning_content:
The most recent release healthy in production is v2.3.0. Note the deployment list has seq ordering — v2.3.1-rc is staging, unhealthy, but not production. So rollback target: v2.3.0.

Wait — there's a subtlety. Is there a trap here? The "most recent release that was healthy in production" = v2.3.0. Rollback to v2.3.0 doesn't require change-manager approval because it has been healthy in production before. Good.

Let me rollback.

Actually, should I roll back before creating the incident? Both fine. Do rollback first, then create incident.

Also note: the deployment list says seq: v2.3.1 has seq 3 and v2.3.1-rc has seq 2 (staging). So ordering by seq: v2.2.9 → v2.3.0 → v2.3.1-rc (staging) → v2.3.1. So v2.3.0 is indeed the latest healthy production release.

Let me rollback and then verify status, then create incident.

transcript.content: The rollback partially failed — it halted after us-east. Let me check the current state.
transcript.reasoning_content: The rollback had a partial failure: halted after us-east. Let's check status.

transcript.content: The rollback is now in a mixed state: us-east on v2.3.0, us-west and eu-west still on v2.3.1. Retrying the rollback to complete it — v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production, so no change-manager approval is required.
transcript.reasoning_content:
The rollback is stuck in a mixed state: us-east on v2.3.0, others on v2.3.1. I should retry the rollback to v2.3.0. v2.3.0 was previously healthy in production, so it's not a "version that has never been healthy in production" — policy approval not needed.

Let me retry the rollback.

transcript.content: Rollback completed across all regions. Verifying health before opening the incident:
transcript.reasoning_content: Now verify health, then create the incident.

transcript.content: Service is healthy again (error rate 0.2%). Now opening the SEV2 incident:
transcript.reasoning_content:
Healthy, error rate 0.2%. Now open SEV2 incident describing what I did.

I should not use an idempotency key shared incorrectly... use a key. This is a fresh incident creation, one call.
